definitions.explanation: A married couple who are both elderly. Often used warmly to describe a couple who have been together for a long time.

examples.japanese: {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つないで⟦{歩|ある}いていた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: An elderly couple was walking hand in hand.

examples.japanese: ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}む→住む：00673_sumu⟧{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: The elderly couple living next door get along very well.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{五十|ごじゅう}→五十：00930_gojuu⟧⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦{以上|いじょう}→以上：01308_ijou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{暮|く}らして→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧きたそうだ。
examples.english: I hear that elderly couple has lived together for over fifty years.

notes:
{老夫婦|ろうふうふ} refers to a married couple who are both elderly, typically implying they have been together for many years.

FORMS:
{老|ろう} (old, elderly) + ⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧ (married couple).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{暮|く}らす→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧: an elderly couple lives (together)
- ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧{老夫婦|ろうふうふ}: a close/loving elderly couple
- {老夫婦|ろうふうふ}{二人暮|ふたりぐ}らし: an elderly couple living alone together

USAGE:
Generally a neutral or warm term. In stories and narratives, {老夫婦|ろうふうふ} often evokes long companionship, quiet lives, or touching devotion. It appears frequently in folktales (e.g., ⟦おじいさん→おじいさん：02860_ojiisan⟧とおばあさん scenes).

- {若夫婦|わかふうふ}: young married couple
